text: At 79', Westport Albion implemented a tactical shift to protect their 3-2 lead by reducing pressing intensity from 0.45 to 0.25 and lowering their defensive line height equivalently, triggering a rest-defense mechanism focused on compactness rather than active ball recovery [#1459]. This change also lowered the team’s tempo from 0.5 to 0.35, indicating a move away from their direct, vertical passing towards a slower, more controlled buildup aimed at managing game tempo [#1459]. Consequently, Westport's PPDA rose from 4.4 to 7.6, signaling a significant drop in pressing aggressiveness, which allowed Kingsmoor FC to increase their expected goals from 0 to 0.92 by exploiting field tilt, especially through wide crossing play, and increasing box touches against Westport's deeper block [#1459]. This tactical trade-off emphasizes Westport’s prioritization of defensive solidity over offensive progression in the match's closing phase.
